history.summary: Ancient Shiva temple on the Grand Trunk Road at Belur/Bally, Howrah (16 G.T. Road, 711201), close to Belur Math, with the Hooghly river nearby. Said to be 400-600 years old; local tradition says the area was once dense forest and a local king or zamindar donated land after a dream, with Dayaram Bose building a small temple and appointing four Brahmin sebayit families. Closely associated with Ramakrishna Paramahamsa, who visited frequently (including with Swami Vivekananda and Swami Brahmananda) and is said to have experienced ecstasy there; Ramakrishna Mission monks still visit regularly, including on Mondays. CSV TOWN FLAG: CSV says town 'Howrah' (the district); the temple is actually at Belur/Bally, Howrah district. Note: Wikipedia's 'Kaleshwar Mandir' article on this Bally temple carries an incongruous Himachal reference - treat age/history claims as tradition, not verified.

name: Baba Kalyaneshwar Temple
town_description: Bally (with Belur) is a town in Howrah district, West Bengal, on the west bank of the Hooghly river, famed for Belur Math and the historic Bally Khal. A busy suburb of Greater Kolkata straddling the Grand Trunk Road.

travel.airport: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport, Kolkata (~14 km)
travel.railway: Bally railway station ~0.7 km; Belur and Belur Math stations nearby on the Howrah-Bandel line
travel.road: 16 Grand Trunk Road, Belur, Bally, Howrah 711201; buses and autos along G.T. Road; ~2.8 km from Noapara metro side.

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Maha Shivaratri and Mondays are busiest.
